name: Georgia Senate Page Program
org: Georgia State Senate (Office of the Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of the Senate)
what_you_do: Serve for one legislative day at the State Capitol. Pages carry messages to senators on the Senate floor. They also watch votes and meet lawmakers.
who_can_apply: Students ages 12 to 18. The packet says there are no exceptions to the minimum age. A page is sponsored by the Lieutenant Governor or one Senator.
pay_detail: $20.00 honorarium paid at the end of the day, plus a certificate of service (2025 welcome packet). A 2026 amount is not posted, so confirm it.
duration: One legislative day. Report about 1.5 hours before the Senate convenes. The Senate usually convenes at 10:00 AM (check the Senate schedule the night before).
deadline_text: Last cycle: applications for the 2026 session opened Dec 15, 2025. The session began Jan 12, 2026. No deadline is listed. 2027 dates are not posted.
how_to_apply: Apply one way only. Lieutenant Governor: fill out the interest form, list three dates, and email it to denese.sampson@ltgov.ga.gov at least one week ahead. Senator: contact that Senator's office. Staff contact: kim.campbell@senate.ga.gov or illana.burkhart@senate.ga.gov, 404-657-7004.
notes: Sources are the 2025 Senate Page welcome packet and the Lieutenant Governor's page, as of Nov 3, 2026. The pages on legis.ga.gov only showed a loading screen. Under Georgia law cited in the packet (O.C.G.A. 20-2-692) page service counts as present at school. Dress code is business or business casual. Cell phones are not allowed while paging. The Georgia House has its own page program at legis.ga.gov/house/page-program, which could not be read.
